title: Light aircraft
object: Four-seat, high-wing, single-engine light aircraft in general arrangement, forward fuselage in section
idea: How an aeroplane holds itself up: lift must equal weight, and the wing stalls when it cannot
summary: Lift is ½ρV²S·C_L and in steady flight it must equal n·W. Slow down and the wing needs more C_L, so the elevator raises the angle of attack until C_L,max, taken from the class's published stall speeds, runs out: the stall. Flaps raise C_L,max and lower the stall speed; a 60° bank doubles the lift needed and raises it by √2.
usedFor: Flight training and physics teaching: the lift equation, angle of attack, stall speed, flaps and load factor in a turn
An atlas entry point: every system of the aeroplane opens its own drawing
Reading a general-arrangement drawing: stations, datum, CG range, third-angle projection
